description.en: Equatorial Guinea's public holidays are established by law to celebrate its independence, political foundations, and strong Roman Catholic tradition. These holidays involve closures of public offices, educational institutions, and many local businesses.

sections.title: About Equatorial Guinea
sections.content: Equatorial Guinea, officially the Republic of Equatorial Guinea, is a country on the west coast of Central Africa. It has an area of 28,000 square kilometres (11,000 sq mi). Formerly the colony of Spanish Guinea, its post-independence name refers to its location both near the Equator and in the African region of Guinea. As of 2025, the country has a population of 1,853,559, over 85% of whom are members of the Fang people, the country's dominant ethnic group. The Bubi people, indigenous to Bioko, are the second largest group at approximately 6.5% of the population. Its capital is Ciudad de la Paz, while its largest city is Bata.

sections.title: How Public Holidays Are Observed in Equatorial Guinea
sections.content: On public holidays, government offices and public schools are closed, and banks/financial institutions typically close. Private businesses may operate reduced hours. Travel activity often increases around major religious and national holidays.

sections.title: Why Equatorial Guinea’s Public Holidays Matter
sections.content: Knowing Equatorial Guinea’s public holidays helps with business planning and payroll management, school and academic scheduling, and travel/accommodation planning. Both residents and visitors benefit from understanding when services may be unavailable.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in Equatorial Guinea?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in Equatorial Guinea?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in Equatorial Guinea?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in Equatorial Guinea?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in Equatorial Guinea?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
